title: AI for Legal, Procurement, and Compliance

questions.question: What boundary should legal and procurement AI workflows preserve?
options: AI can take the negotiation position once the clause register has been fully populated
AI can prepare and structure work, but humans own interpretation, negotiation, and decisions
AI can accept residual risk on routine contracts, escalating only the unusual clauses
AI can issue the final review note, provided the source document was internally approved — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
questions.explanation: AI support does not remove accountable legal or procurement review. The model may structure information, but interpretation, risk acceptance, and negotiation positions stay with humans.

questions.question: What three risks does this lesson name for an AI-generated summary of a contract?
options: It cites the wrong jurisdiction, misdates the term, or misstates the governing language, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
It runs too slowly, costs more per document, or cannot handle scanned contract formats
It drops the formatting, reorders the clauses, or loses the numbering of the annexes
It misses obligations, weakens the negotiation position, or exposes confidential material
questions.explanation: The lesson names exactly these three risks. That is why confidentiality and obligation risk have to be checked before a generated summary is used.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A signed contract once both parties have accepted the compared terms
A final legal opinion on the obligations found in the source document
A ranked legal and procurement review plan with controls and rationale
A vendor approval that clears the supplier for the procurement process without further review
questions.explanation: The artifact structures review preparation. It is not a legal decision - human reviewers remain accountable for interpretation and approval.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: An obligation list generated once and reused across later vendor comparisons unchanged
A review step that is skipped for policies the compliance team already knows
A decision record that captures the outcome but not the evidence behind it
A clause register that keeps key terms traceable back to the source document
questions.explanation: A clause register keeps key terms traceable. Confidentiality checks, a named legal reviewer, and a decision record with its evidence are the other controls this lesson teaches.

questions.question: When should legal or procurement AI work require a launch gate?
options: When obligation risk, confidential terms, or missing evidence create high impact
Only when the source document runs longer than the model's context window
Only when an external vendor rather than an internal policy is being reviewed — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Only when the summary will be forwarded outside the legal team that made it
questions.explanation: High-risk generated review work needs explicit human review, triggered by obligation risk, confidentiality, and missing evidence rather than by document length.

questions.question: What should vendor-term summaries remain linked to?
options: The model's own wording, so the summary stays internally consistent, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
The source clauses and the evidence the review was actually based on
The prompt that produced it, so the same output can be regenerated
The standard template the procurement team uses for every supplier
questions.explanation: Traceability protects legal and procurement decisions: vendor terms need evidence that leads back to the source clauses.
